title: Containing Agent Chaos — Solomon Hykes, Dagger
talk_summary: Solomon Hykes argues that scaling coding agents requires giving each agent an isolated, customizable, multiplayer environment rather than either YOLO shared-workspace mode or opaque background PR services. He demos 'container use': an MCP-integrated tool where agents create ephemeral containers and snapshot state into git objects, so a human can inspect, diff, merge, or discard each agent's work without polluting the workspace.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent ephemeral container environments with git-backed snapshots
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent action runs in an ephemeral container; file/container state is snapshotted into special git objects alongside the repo, so the agent's work is isolated from the human workspace and can be diffed, merged, or thrown away.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every time an action needs to be taken, there's an ephemeral container running and then being snapshotted

takeaways.technique: Parallel experiment branches from a shared base state
takeaways.what_they_do: After merging a base environment, the speaker spawns multiple agents (Claude, Goose) from that same state to try variants in parallel, each on its own branch, then diffs and picks a winner.
takeaways.evidence_quote: since the environment is now in this state, I can ask for help from a few other agents

takeaways.technique: Environment provisioning exposed to agents via MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent is given MCP tools to create and configure its own container environment (e.g. pick Go version), so it self-provisions a repeatable build/test environment instead of the human pre-configuring it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent is given the ability to figure out what environment it needs and then configure that but in a repeatable containerized way

takeaways.what_they_do: Secrets are plugged into a specific environment from the user's own password manager (1Password), so only that environment can use them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this environment gets this secret and boom, it can use it

takeaways.technique: Human-in-the-loop via inspectable snapshot history, not PR review
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of watching every tool call or waiting on a PR, the human inspects the agent's git-log-like snapshot history and merges the state they like — a middle-ground collaboration loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's not watching every tool and wrecking a shared environment, but it's not waiting for a pull request
